topic: Neural Network Learning and Intuitive Backpropagation
target_audience: University students and aspiring AI practitioners

sections.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn by adjusting internal parameters called weights.
Think of weights as dials on a machine.
Tuning these dials helps the network produce correct outputs.
animations: Create a simple neural network diagram with nodes on left (inputs) connected to a node on right (output). Label connections 'Weights' in #FFFFFF.
Animate 'Flour' and 'Sugar' icons (#FFD700) entering the input nodes from the left.
Show a rotating dial icon (#00FF00) over the connection lines to symbolize adjustment.
Scale the 'Weights' text labels while the dial icon rotates to indicate changing values.
Transform a 'Burnt Cookie' icon (#8B4513) at the output into a 'Perfect Cookie' (#F5DEB3).

sections.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
lecture_lines: Inputs enter the network and travel from left to right.
Each input is multiplied by a weight.
Weighted values are summed at each neuron.
An activation function acts as a gatekeeper for signals.
The final output is the network's current prediction.
animations: Show input values like '350' and '10' in #ADD8E6 appearing on the left side of the screen.
Animate lines with labels 'x Weight' (#FF69B4) connecting these inputs to a central 'Gatekeeper' node.
Pulse the 'Gatekeeper' node in #FF4500 and reveal the 'Burnt Cookie' prediction value on the right.

sections.title: The Loss Function: Measuring the Mistake
lecture_lines: To improve, we must measure how wrong we are.
The loss function calculates the distance from the truth.
High loss means a large error in the prediction.
animations: Display 'Prediction' (#FF0000) and 'Target' (#00FF00) as two distinct points on a vertical scale.
Draw a double-headed arrow (#FFFFE0) between the two points and label it 'Distance'.
Show the formula 'Error = Prediction - Target' in #FFFFFF at the top of the screen.

sections.title: Backpropagation: The Blame Game
lecture_lines: Backpropagation traces the error back through the network.
We calculate how much each weight contributed to error.
The chain rule helps calculate these sensitivities precisely.
This assigns "blame" to specific dials in the system.
We now know which direction to turn each dial.
animations: Highlight the 'Error Score' in #FF0000 with a flashing effect to draw attention.
Animate arrows moving backward from the Error towards the Weights to show the flow of blame.
Color the 'Timer Weight' dark red (#8B0000) and 'Temp Weight' light red (#FA8072) based on contribution.
Display the mathematical symbol for the gradient 'dError/dWeight' in #00FFFF near the weights.
Highlight the weight with the highest error contribution using a glowing #FFFFFF border.

sections.title: Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill
lecture_lines: The loss landscape is like a hilly, foggy terrain.
The gradient points in the steepest uphill direction.
We take a small step in the opposite direction.
This process iteratively moves the network toward minimum error.
Walking downhill reduces the overall cost of our model.
animations: Draw a smooth U-shaped curve in #FFFFFF representing the 'Loss Landscape'.
Place a small 'Robot Chef' dot (#FFD700) at a high position on the slope.
Draw a vector arrow (#00FF00) pointing down the slope from the dot's current position.
Animate the dot moving one small 'step' down the curve in the direction of the arrow.
Fade in the text 'Minimum Error' in #00FF00 at the lowest point of the curve.

sections.title: The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect
lecture_lines: Learning requires repeating this cycle thousands of times.
Each pass nudges the weights closer to perfection.
Practice eventually transforms a random guess into accuracy.
animations: Show a circular arrow (#00BFFF) rotating around the steps: Forward, Loss, and Backprop.
Animate a line graph showing the 'Error' value starting high and steadily decreasing.
Display the text 'Golden Recipe' in gold (#FFD700) at the center once the error is low.
